newsitem.title: GERMANY: North German sugar firms plan autumn 1997 merger.
newsitem.headline: North German sugar firms plan autumn 1997 merger.

text.p: Four northern German sugar companies have decided to put a merger bid to the vote at shareholders' meetings in September 1997, a joint statement issued by Zuckerverbund Nord AG (ZVN) said.

The envisaged new company, Nordzucker AG, with annual turnover of around two billion marks, would become Europe's third largest sugar producer after Germany's Suedzucker AG and Franco-Italian Eridania Beghin-Say.

Representatives of the four firms at a June 13 meeting decided focusing the activities and performances of the four companies and their subsidiaries would be in the best interest of shareholders and farmers, the statement said.
The merger would involve ZVN, Union-Zucker Suedhannover GmbH, Zuckerfabrik Harsum AG and Zucker AG Uelzen-Braunschweig and a total of five subsidiaries.
